paragraphs.source_en: “As for those people you look down on, whatever they say, why not simply pay no attention to them? After all, it is all just nonsense. Is it worth losing your temper over those middle-school boys? What is that? They are deliberately disturbing you? But even if you negotiate with them and quarrel with them, will they not go right on disturbing you just the same? On that point, I think the Japanese of old were far superior to Westerners. These days it is fashionable to say that whatever Westerners do is positive and active, but in fact there is a great flaw in that. To begin with, this so-called positiveness implies no end; even if one goes on acting positively forever, one can never arrive at satisfaction or perfection. Suppose there is a cypress tree across the way, and because it obstructs your view you cut it down; then the lodging house beyond blocks the view, so you have that removed, and then the next house behind it becomes offensive to the eye. Is that not endless? Everything Westerners do is like that. Neither Napoleon nor Alexander, not one of them, was ever satisfied with the victories he had won. Someone displeases you, so you quarrel; the other party will not submit, so you take him to court; you win the case. Do you suppose that will bring you peace? It will not! Until death you remain forever in a state of restless agitation, and you never gain peace of mind. Oligarchy is no good, so one changes to representative government; representative government is thought no good, so one wants to devise something new again. A river looks objectionable, so a bridge is built; a mountain seems troublesome, so a tunnel is dug; walking on two legs is inconvenient, so railways are laid. Satisfaction cannot be attained that way. But then again, human beings being what they are, to what extent can they actively force things to conform to their own wishes? Western civilization may be active and enterprising, but after all it is a civilization created by people who spend their whole lives dissatisfied. Japanese civilization does not seek satisfaction by changing the world outside oneself. Where it differs greatly from the West is that it developed on the fundamental assumption that the surrounding circumstances are not to be moved. Take the relation between parents and children: even if it is not pleasant, people do not, like Europeans, try to alter that relation in order to obtain peace; rather, they regard the existing relation between parent and child as immovable, and seek means of mental composure within that relation. It is the same with husband and wife, lord and retainer; the same with the distinction between samurai and townsman; the same in the way nature itself is regarded. If a mountain lies between you and the neighboring province so that you cannot go there, you look for various ways to live well without going there, instead of thinking about cutting through the mountain and making a road. That is to say, one cultivates a state of mind that is just as satisfied without crossing the mountain. Therefore, think about it: Zenists and Confucians alike always grasp this point at the root. No matter how remarkable one may be, the world can never be made entirely as one wishes.

paragraphs.source_zh: “那些你瞧不起的人，他们说什么，你不理他们不就行了吗？反正都是一些无聊的事儿嘛。和那些中学生怄气值得吗？你说什么？他们故意搅扰你？不过，你就是和他们交涉，和他们争吵，结果还不是照旧来搅扰你吗？我觉得在这点上，古时候的日本人要比西洋人强得多。最近流行的是，认为西洋人做什么事都是积极的，其实，这里边存在着很大的缺陷。先说所谓积极的，这就意味着无止境，即便是永远积极地干下去，也不可能达到满意的境地或完全的境地。比如对面有棵柏树，嫌它妨碍视野，于是斫伐掉，可是前边的公寓又会挡住视线，让公寓拆除，后边的另一栋房子又会看着不顺眼，这岂不是永无止境吗？西洋人所干的事儿，都是这样嘛。拿破仑也好，亚历山大也好，没有一个人是满足于已取得的胜利的。看别人不顺眼，于是争吵，对方不服，到法院打官司，打赢了，你认为这样就会得到安宁了吗？不会的！一直到死总是处在焦躁不安之中，永远不会得到精神的安宁。寡头政治不好，于是改为代议政治，认为代议政治不行，于是又想搞出什么新鲜的东西来。看着河不顺眼，于是架桥，看着山别扭，于是挖隧道，两脚走路费事，于是修铁路，这样是不可能得到满足的。可是话得说回来，人嘛，究竟能够积极地按自己意愿到多大程度呢？西方的文明，也许是积极的、进取的，但它毕竟是由一辈子都活在不满足当中的人们创造出来的。日本的文明，决不是除自己之外，用改变外部世界的办法来求得满足。它与西方大不相同之处，是在周围的环境根本不可动摇的一大假定的前提下发展起来的。就以父母与子女的关系而言，即使不融洽，也决不会像欧洲人那样去改变这种关系来求得安宁，而是认为已有的双亲与子女的关系是不可动摇的，只能在这种关系之中来寻求心理平静的手段。夫妻、君臣的关系也是如此，武士与町人的区别，也是如此，在如何看待大自然上，也是这样。如果有山相隔，不能到邻接的地区去，人们就去寻找即使不到邻接地区去也能照样活得好的种种办法，而不是去考虑如何开山修路。这就是说，要养成不翻山越岭同样也很满足的精神状态。因此，你想想看，禅家也好，儒家也好，总是从根本上掌握这一点的。不管自己如何了不起，人世毕竟是不能尽人意的。

paragraphs.source_en: You cannot pull back the setting sun, nor can you make the Kamo River flow upstream. All you can work on is your own mind; if only you train it well and make it free, then no matter how wildly the students of Rakuunkan behave, surely you can remain unconcerned. With those sly fellows you would simply ignore them accordingly; as for the nonsense of such uncultivated fellows, all you need do is calmly call them ‘damned fools’ and be done with it, is it not? They say that in old times, when a monk was about to be cut down by someone, he composed a wonderfully apt verse: ‘In the flash of lightning, I cut the spring wind.’ Very likely only after accumulating discipline of the mind and reaching the utmost limit of passivity could one utter such a keen and extraordinary saying. A person like me, of course, cannot yet understand such profound principles. In any case, the idea that only Western-style activism is good seems rather mistaken. Take you, for instance: however actively you try to conduct yourself, can you do anything about those students coming to make sport of you? If you had the power to shut that school down, or if the other side had done something bad enough for you to complain to the police, that would be another matter; but if not, then no matter how much you practice activism, you will never win. If you take an active line, you run into the question of money, and you run into the question of being one against many; in other words, you would have to bow your head to the rich, and you would have to submit to those children who rely on their numbers. For a poor man like you, and alone besides, wanting to fight actively is precisely the source of your discontent. Well then, do you understand?”

units.source_en: You cannot pull back the setting sun, nor can you make the Kamo River flow upstream.
units.source_zh: 你既不能把落日拉回来，也不能使加茂河倒流回来。

units.source_en: All you can work on is your own mind; if only you train it well and make it free, then no matter how wildly the students of Rakuunkan behave, surely you can remain unconcerned.
units.source_zh: 所能做到的只是在自己的心上下工夫，只要把心修炼好，使它能得自由，那落云馆的学生不管怎样胡闹，你不是就可以满不在乎了吗？

units.source_en: With those sly fellows you would simply ignore them accordingly; as for the nonsense of such uncultivated fellows, all you need do is calmly call them ‘damned fools’ and be done with it, is it not?

ja.t: わんでおられそうなものだ。ぴん

units.source_zh: 对于那些狡诈的家伙，你就会相应不理，对于那种没有教养的家伙的胡说八道，你只要无动于衷地骂他们一声‘这帮王八蛋’不就完事儿了吗？

units.source_zh: 据说过去有个和尚，当别人将要杀他的时候，他做了一个很妙的偈语：‘电光影里斩春风’。

units.source_en: Very likely only after accumulating discipline of the mind and reaching the utmost limit of passivity could one utter such a keen and extraordinary saying.

ja.t: るのじゃないかしらん。

units.source_zh: 这很可能是在累积了心的修炼，达到消极的极点之后，才能说出这样精辟卓绝的话来吧。

units.source_en: A person like me, of course, cannot yet understand such profound principles.

ja.t: なんか、そんなむずかしい

units.source_zh: 像我这种人，当然还不可能了解这种深奥的道理。

units.source_en: In any case, the idea that only Western-style activism is good seems rather mistaken.
units.source_zh: 总之，那种认为只有西方式的积极主义好的想法，是不太对头的。

units.source_en: Take you, for instance: however actively you try to conduct yourself, can you do anything about those students coming to make sport of you?

ja.t: をひやかしにくるのをどうする

units.source_zh: 就拿你来说，不管你怎样按积极主义去处世，那些学生们来捉弄你，你不还是毫无办法吗？

units.source_en: If you had the power to shut that school down, or if the other side had done something bad enough for you to complain to the police, that would be another matter; but if not, then no matter how much you practice activism, you will never win.
units.source_zh: 如果你有权势把那个学校封门，或者对方做了足以使你到警察那里去告状的坏事，那又当别论，如果不是那样，你就是怎样奉行积极主义，也不会取胜的啊。

units.source_en: If you take an active line, you run into the question of money, and you run into the question of being one against many; in other words, you would have to bow your head to the rich, and you would have to submit to those children who rely on their numbers. For a poor man like you, and alone besides, wanting to fight actively is precisely the source of your discontent.
units.source_zh: 如果你搞积极主义，就会碰上金钱的问题，就会碰上势孤力单的问题，换句话说，你就得向有钱的人低头，你就得听命于人多势众的那些孩子们，像你这样穷光蛋，又只是孤零零的一个人，想要积极地去较量，这点正是你不满的根源嘛。

units.source_en: Well then, do you understand?”
units.source_zh: 怎么样，你懂了没有？”

paragraphs.source_zh: 你既不能把落日拉回来，也不能使加茂河倒流回来。所能做到的只是在自己的心上下工夫，只要把心修炼好，使它能得自由，那落云馆的学生不管怎样胡闹，你不是就可以满不在乎了吗？对于那些狡诈的家伙，你就会相应不理，对于那种没有教养的家伙的胡说八道，你只要无动于衷地骂他们一声‘这帮王八蛋’不就完事儿了吗？据说过去有个和尚，当别人将要杀他的时候，他做了一个很妙的偈语：‘电光影里斩春风’。这很可能是在累积了心的修炼，达到消极的极点之后，才能说出这样精辟卓绝的话来吧。像我这种人，当然还不可能了解这种深奥的道理。总之，那种认为只有西方式的积极主义好的想法，是不太对头的。就拿你来说，不管你怎样按积极主义去处世，那些学生们来捉弄你，你不还是毫无办法吗？如果你有权势把那个学校封门，或者对方做了足以使你到警察那里去告状的坏事，那又当别论，如果不是那样，你就是怎样奉行积极主义，也不会取胜的啊。如果你搞积极主义，就会碰上金钱的问题，就会碰上势孤力单的问题，换句话说，你就得向有钱的人低头，你就得听命于人多势众的那些孩子们，像你这样穷光蛋，又只是孤零零的一个人，想要积极地去较量，这点正是你不满的根源嘛。怎么样，你懂了没有？”
